newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's EPR rebels say their fight goes on.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's EPR rebels say their fight goes on.

text.p: Leftist Mexican rebels, whose month-long truce in the troubled southern state of Guerrero is about to end, said on Saturday that they would continue their struggle.
In a statement made available to Reuters, the guerrillas of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) said they were committed to a "larger struggle to achieve the changes the nation requires".
"All forms of struggle must come together to this end, so the (rebels) will continue to encourage it and will continue responding with armed self-defence," the statement said.
While not clearly stating that the truce would end as previously announced at 8.30 p.m. Sunday (0230 GMT Monday), the rebels made clear that they consider themselves as a combatant force.
The EPR used the term "armed self-defence" to describe their coordinated attacks on military and police in several states in late August which left 17 people dead.
In the statement, the rebels also rejected any negotiations with the government. "We will not negotiate with those who are guilty of death, deceit and repression," the EPR said.
The government has for its part ruled out any peace talks with the rebels, calling them "terrorists" and pledging to hunt them down.
By contrast, the government and the separate Zapatista rebels in the southeastern state of Chiapas have been in on-again, off-again peace efforts for the last 18 months.

The EPR called its truce so that local elections in Guerrero state, one of Mexico's poorest and most violent despite hosting the world-famous tourist resort of Acapulco, could be carried out unimpeded earlier this month.

The leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) made important gains in the elections at the cost of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which nevertheless won the lion's share of municipalities and seats in the state congress.
The EPR said it believed its presence in Guerrero -- where it first appeared on June 28 -- had helped encourage people to vote against the PRI.
Tension has mounted in Guerrero in past days as the deadline for the EPR truce to end approached.

The army has stepped up its presence in the state, with patrols and roadblocks increasing. Reporters this week saw elite troops with black berets and painted faces patrolling rural areas this week as military helicopters and planes buzzed overhead.
